meta.methodology: Read framework.md, torah_76_packages.json, all reference===76 edges from torahData.js, and the full source text torah_76.txt. Scanned every line for explicit bechina markers: בְּחִינַת (used as identity declaration, not directional), הַיְנוּ (used as equivalence/explanatory identity), נִקְרָא. Each candidate was checked against the dataset. Only bechina statements establishing a structural identity between two concept-nodes were counted. Directional eitza usages of בְּחִינַת (e.g., 'on account of X comes Y') and purely narrative descriptions were excluded.

Though ראיה is the unifying concept of Package 1, and חידוש המוח represents the positive outcome of גדלות (Package 3), the explicit bechina statement 'חידוש המוח הוא בחינת ראיה' places it in Package 1 as a bechina of the vision cluster. additions.reason: Lines 8-9 use 'בְּחִינַת' to introduce a state: 'יֵשׁ בְּחִינַת צָמְאָה נַפְשִׁי' and 'זֶה בְּחִינַת צִמָּאוֹן כַּנַּ״ל'. Tzima'on (unquenched thirst, unregulated spiritual longing) is described as a bechina — a state or mode of being. The Rebbe then explains it is the negative pole counterpart to ראיה/גבול וזמן: instead of seeing with proper limits, one is 'thirsting' without time and without sekhel — 'בְּלֹא זְמַן וָשֵׂכֶל'. In the Torah's polarity structure, tzima'on represents the absence of vision (=Package 1's positive pole) — it is the Package 1 evil mirror: unguided spiritual longing that lacks the structure of seeing. Polarity is evil in context: tzima'on in this Torah is the problematic state of undirected, boundless religious activity without the regulating structure of ראיה/גבול. Assignment to Package 1 (not Package 2) because tzima'on's essential nature is the absence of ראיה — it is the negative face of the vision domain, not the constrained-intellect domain.

concepts_examined_and_excluded.reason: Line 9: 'שֶׁאֶזְכֶּה שֶׁתִּהְיֶה הָעֲבוֹדָה בִּבְחִינַת רְאִיָּה'. The phrase 'בִּבְחִינַת רְאִיָּה' here means 'in the mode/form of vision', used directionally — it describes the aspirational goal state of worship. This is a conditional/directional usage ('may I merit that the worship be IN the mode of ראיה') rather than a symmetric identity declaration ('X IS a bechina of Y'). The underlying equation ראיה = גבול וזמן is covered by the חידוש המוח and ידיעת השכל additions above. Excluded to avoid duplicating the ראיה-cluster additions.

Lines 14-15 discuss תשובה מאהבה extensively. The Rebbe does say that through תשובה מאהבה one attains שכל צח and גדלות המחין. However, this is consistently framed as eitza (cause → effect): 'אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהִתְפַּלֵּל בְּשֵׂכֶל צַח עַד שֶׁיָּשׁוּב... מֵאַהֲבָה'. The text never says 'תשובה מאהבה הוא בחינת גדלות המחין' or any symmetric identity. It is strictly a causal agent (eitza), not a bechina identity. It also appears in the dataset as eitza edges (e.g., line 17224). Excluded.

The phrase 'הוּא בְּחִינַת אַחַר הַדְּבָרִים' here refers back to the verb phrase 'speaking before the mind rises' as an instance of אחר הדברים. However, 'speech before thought' is a description/example illustrating the state of קטנות המחין, not a new concept-node forming an independent bechina. The node אחר הדברים is already in the dataset (edge 1757). This is a contextual illustration, not a new concept addition.

Line 13: 'וְאֵל הוּא חֶסֶד'. This is a Talmudic proof-text citation (Berakhot 33a via Psalm 52:3) used to support the equation of גדלות המחין with חסדים ורחמים. The word 'אֵל' is equated with חֶסֶד as a divine attribute. However, this equation is used as a supporting citation within the already-established bechina (גדלות ↔ רחמים וחסדים, which IS in the dataset as edge 2736). Introducing 'חסד' and 'אל' as separate new concept-nodes would create redundancy with the already-captured nodes and would import Talmudic-citation nodes rather than Torah-76-specific bechina nodes. Excluded.
